question: Would a distant observer really see someone falling into a black hole hang frozen at its edge forever?
answer: Only in principle. Her light is stretched and dimmed faster and faster as she nears the horizon: at a black hole of 10 solar masses, its wavelength more than doubles every fifth of a millisecond. Light arrives in photons, so one of them is the last. The frozen figure goes black in a blink.
move: A process that never quite ends can still be over in practice.
reference: Misner, Thorne & Wheeler, Gravitation, W. H. Freeman, 1973
